newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon would split to facilitate merger.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon would split to facilitate merger.

text.p: Raytheon Co is looking to merge its defense operations with a competitor in such a way as to avoid either company paying taxes on the deal, published reports said Friday.

Citing remarks by Raytheon Chief Financial Officer Peter D'Angelo to analysts in New York, the Boston Globe and Boston Herald said the Lexington, Mass.-based company was willing to split itself between its defense and commerical businesses.
"Basically, it seems to be prepared to surrender control of its defense business as part of a consolidation," BT Securities analyst Wolfgang Demisch said.
Raytheon spokesmen declined comment on the remarks.

Analysts have said that since last week's news of Boeing Co's acquisition of McDonnell Douglas Corp, Raytheon has come under increasing pressure to merge with GM Hughes Electronics Corp or another big defense contractor.

Those who attended the Raytheon dinner with analysts Wednesday in New York told the Globe that D'Angelo did not specify which companies Raytheon was talking to, but he said any combination of the remaining big defense contractors was possible.
Raytheon Chief Executive Officer Dennis Picard also declined to discuss acquisition plans.

J.P. Morgan analyst Roger Threlfall, who was not immediately available for comment, told the Globe that D'Angelo said voting control was less important to Raytheon than some of what the CFO said were "social issues" -- deciding how to consolidate plants and work forces.
"It was clear, and I interpreted it this way, that they will not hang their Massachusetts work force out to dry just so they can get a deal," Threlfall said.
Raytheon, in addition to its defense program, has huge investments in engineering and construction, aircraft and appliances.
